stories.headline: Eritrea cuts diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after diplomat expulsions and rebel support claims
stories.body:
Eritrea cut all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia on Thursday following a growing political dispute [c2].

The decision came after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats from its capital, Addis Ababa [c2]. Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata [c3]. These diplomats included the charge d'affaires and officials accredited to the African Union [c3]. Ethiopia gave the 10 diplomats 48 hours to leave the country [c3].

The official break in diplomatic ties occurred on October 1, 2026 [c1]. Both countries accused each other of stoking internal conflicts [c1]. Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of backing a new rebel alliance [c4]. Ethiopia said these countries are supporting an opposition group led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front [c4].

Eritrea denied these claims [c11]. Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said Eritrea is not backing the newly formed rebel alliance [c11]. The opposition coalition against Ethiopia's federal government includes several armed groups [c8]. It includes the Tigray People's Liberation Front and the Oromo Liberation Army [c8]. It also includes a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front [c8]. Militant groups from Benishangul-Gumuz and Afar have joined the alliance as well [c8].

Fighting has continued to cause civilian deaths in the region [c9]. A medic in the southern Tigrayan town of Alamata reported that 52 civilians died during three days of heavy fighting [c9]. In response to rising security concerns, Ethiopian security services took new measures [c12]. Ethiopia's National Intelligence and Security Service announced an indefinite ban on drone flights [c12]. This ban applies to Addis Ababa and surrounding areas [c12].

The conflict comes after a history of long tension and changing relations between the two nations [c5]. Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962 [c5]. Eritrea secured its independence in 1993 [c5]. President Isaias Afwerki led an armed struggle that won independence for Eritrea [c5]. Relations improved when Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came to power in 2018 [c6]. Abiy moved to normalise diplomatic relations with President Afwerki [c6].

Later, a major civil war broke out inside Ethiopia [c7]. The civil war lasted two years between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front [c7]. An African Union mediator estimated that 600,000 lives were lost during the civil war between 2020 and 2022 [c10]. The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended that civil war [c7]. Now, new fighting and accusations have broken the peace between the two neighboring countries [c1].

vocab.meaning: relating to official relations between countries
took control of another territory and added it to one's own
a group of political or military parties working together

stories.headline: French prime minister holds crisis meeting as student protests cause widespread violence
stories.body:
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday over spreading student unrest [c17].

Nationwide high school protests led to violence and major disruptions [c13]. French police arrested 1,949 people during the protests on Thursday [c13]. The police reported that 305 police officers suffered injuries [c13]. France's interior ministry said student actions affected 1,027 out of 3,700 high schools across the country [c14]. Students set up blockades at 222 high schools [c14]. University students joined the demonstrations on Thursday and blocked access to about 30 university campuses [c15].

Protests turned violent in several cities [c18]. A bin fire at Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes damaged the entrance hall [c18]. In Auchel, the headteacher at Degrugillier high school suffered an ear injury from a firework [c19]. Protesters outside Saint-Exupery high school in Marseille forced firefighters to leave their vehicle before setting the fire truck on fire [c21]. Authorities in Strasbourg ordered tram services to halt after students placed barriers on the tracks [c16].

French National Rally leader Marine Le Pen called for a new anti-rioting law [c20]. Le Pen said the protests were riots organised by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise [c20]. The French government announced that many high schools would switch to online classes [c23]. Education Minister Édouard Geffray scheduled meetings for Friday with unions, parent groups, and student associations [c22]. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez launched an internal police investigation over allegations of excessive force against three students [c24].

vocab.meaning: a state of angry public agitation or protest
claims that someone has done something wrong, made without proof

stories.headline: United States urges European allies to release emergency fuel reserves as prices surge
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged European partners on social media to release emergency diesel reserves immediately [c25].

Fuel prices surged after the start of the US war on Iran [c26]. Average US diesel prices rose over 70 percent to $6.39 per gallon [c26]. US President Donald Trump said he is considering a ban on US diesel exports to lower domestic costs [c27]. European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic warned that an export ban would bring dramatic economic consequences [c29]. Sefcovic said such a ban would be unexpected for Europeans [c29].

In the United Kingdom, the average price of a litre of diesel reached a record 199.72p on Wednesday [c31]. Brent crude oil prices rose above $101 per barrel on Thursday [c32]. Prices stood at about $72 a barrel in February before the Iran war [c32]. British ministers held calls on Thursday with European partners to discuss using emergency reserves [c30]. French President Emmanuel Macron planned a G7 meeting for mid-October to coordinate fuel releases [c28].

Other nations took steps to protect domestic fuel supplies [c33]. PetroChina cancelled October fuel shipments beyond Hong Kong and Macau [c33]. Russia extended its diesel export ban through October 31 [c34]. Refined product shipments through the Strait of Hormuz dropped sharply to 677,000 barrels per day in late September [c36]. Tensions in the strait remained high after three oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Tuesday [c37].

vocab.meaning: supplies kept available for future or emergency use
objects fired or thrown as weapons

stories.headline: Indian pilot praised after surviving cockpit stabbing on Flydubai flight as UAE probes terror link
stories.body:
Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar survived a knife attack inside the cockpit on a flight carrying 174 passengers [c38].

His co-pilot attacked him with a knife during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv [c38]. The attack forced the flight to make an emergency landing in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday [c39]. The plane was Flydubai flight FZ1073 [c53]. It landed safely in Tabuk at 9:45 am local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members [c53].

According to Flightradar24, the aircraft plummeted around 17,000 feet in altitude in one minute during the fight [c47]. Media reports said 166 of the 174 passengers were Israeli citizens [c48]. The suspect accused of attacking the captain is an Omani national [c49]. Machchhar was transferred to Abu Dhabi to recover from his injuries [c40].

World leaders praised the Indian pilot for his bravery [c41]. US President Donald Trump called Machchhar a hero for fighting off the attacker and opening the cockpit door to call for help [c41]. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on X that Machchhar showed immense courage [c42]. Modi added that Machchhar's quick actions prevented another attack like 9/11 [c42]. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised Machchhar on X for saving 174 lives and preventing a disaster [c43]. Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination [c44].

Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said the co-pilot was transferred to the United Arab Emirates on Thursday morning [c46]. An Emirati security team accompanied the co-pilot during the transfer [c46]. The UAE chief prosecutor announced an investigation into the fight [c45]. UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi launched an official probe into whether the attack involved terrorist intent [c55]. Authorities from Saudi Arabia, Israel, the UAE, the US, and Oman are jointly working to determine the motive [c56]. Israeli intelligence and security officials traveled to Saudi Arabia to help with the investigation [c57].

US President Donald Trump said Tehran was likely involved in the flight attack [c50]. Trump warned that Iran would be hit very hard if it was responsible [c50]. Trump also said in an interview with Time magazine that he might resume bombing Iran after November 3 [c51]. The Wall Street Journal reported that the US plans to send up to 10,000 extra troops to the Middle East [c52]. The US will also send a third aircraft carrier by late November [c52]. All 174 passengers later continued their journey to Tel Aviv on a replacement plane [c54]. They departed Saudi Arabia at approximately 5:40 pm on Wednesday [c54].

vocab.meaning: dropped down rapidly at a high speed
the process of teaching a person to accept a set of beliefs uncritically

stories.headline: Election Commission orders probe into bulk voter deletion applications in Karnataka
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India ordered an investigation into bulk voter deletion filings in Karnataka [c62].

The decision followed a five-hour protest by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar [c62]. Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka V. Anbu Kumar directed officials to take action against false Form-7 filings [c63]. Karnataka Police registered five cases on October 1, 2026, over the bulk filings [c64]. Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP and election officials of colluding to delete targeted voters [c65]. Reports showed that many voter deletion filings targeted Muslim voters during the Special Intensive Revision [c68].

In Babaleshwar, 10 individuals submitted 1,363 out of 1,373 Form 7 applications on September 22 [c69]. In Bhalki, 30 people filed over 1,700 deletion applications on September 23 [c70]. Political pressure against election officials grew across India [c67]. Leaders from 21 Opposition parties met in New Delhi on September 30 to plan strategy against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar [c67]. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called Kumar a puppet of government leaders [c72]. Dipke claimed that about 13 crore voters have been deleted from electoral rolls since 2024 [c66]. The Cockroach Janta Party demanded that future elections use paper ballots instead of electronic voting machines [c73]. The Election Commission dismissed claims of internal breakdown and said all commissioners agreed on key decisions [c60].

vocab.meaning: secretly cooperating for an illegal or dishonest purpose
